asleep.text: (Fast asleep. Best not to wake them.)
asleep.speaker: narrator

offer.text: You there. You've got walking legs. Sit. No, don't sit, you'll get comfortable. Listen.

offer2.text: Forty years I walked the Westreach for the post. The old route went the long way round: the west milestone, the lone oak, up Lark Hill, down through Mossgate on the cart track. Nobody uses it now. I want it walked once more and written down before my memory goes the way of my knees.

offer3.text: Good. Take these notes. They're in my handwriting, so good luck. And mind the cart track. Folk used to say it was haunted. It wasn't. It was Tobin's father with a bottle.

route_progress.text: Well? Did you find the milestone? They moved it once, you know. Fifty paces. Nobody asked me.

route_done.text: You walked it. All of it? Even the cart track? ...Who was camped there?

choices.text: Brigands. They won't be back soon.

route_done2.text: Hm. In my day it was just foxes and Tobin's father. Here: this charm was mine for thirty years. Never once late while I wore it. Well. Rarely.

remedy.text: What's that smell? Is that... Hester's brew? Give it here. If it's poison, at least it's local.

choices.text: She says it's a good sign that it smells awful.

remedy2.text: ...Oh. Oh, that's warm. All the way down. Tell Hester she's a menace and I love her.

main.text: Still here? Good. The village needs people who notice things.

choices.text: What did you notice, on the roads?

roads.text: That the post always arrives, and the reasons why it's late are always more interesting than the post.
